problem: Existing navigation memories (explicit maps, RNN states, or topological graphs) either lose fine scene detail or are hard to query for target-relevant cues in unknown environments; implicit NeRF memory has not been used for end-to-end navigation control and suffers from noise in unseen regions.
motivation: Reliable, efficient navigation in unknown environments needs long-term memory of dense scene cues that can be retrieved conditioned on the goal. NeRF gives a dense, differentiable, implicit scene representation, suggesting it can serve as an online memory for control tasks.
key_idea: Store historical scene features online in a NeRF-based implicit memory and retrieve target-relevant cues via a differentiable Dual Space Attention with uncertainty masking to drop low signal-to-noise information.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract claims that the implicit, differentiable structure of NeRF enables target-conditioned retrieval that yields visible target search and orientation behavior, and that uncertainty masking is needed to handle noise in unseen regions and may improve exploration.
method: NeRF scene memory: scene features from historical observations are stored online in a NeRF structure as implicit memory.
Dual Space Attention: a differentiable memory retrieval mechanism that extracts target-relevant scene cues from the NeRF memory to support long-term behavior.
Uncertainty masking: during retrieval, removes low signal-to-noise information caused by lack of environment priors, potentially enhancing exploration.
End-to-end navigation pipeline: the memory and retrieval are integrated into a learned policy for navigation in unknown environments.
